tools.name: CodeQL
tools.language: the github/codeql repo itself is the query-library/docs repo (GitHub labels it language 'CodeQL', i.e. .ql/.qll files); the actual extraction/evaluation engine ships as a SEPARATE closed-source CLI, historically implemented in OCaml + C++
tools.runtime: native CodeQL CLI binary (closed-source) + per-language extractors that hook into each language's real build/compiler (javac, csc, a C/C++ compiler shim, etc.)
storage: a 'CodeQL database' -- a compiled relational representation (TRAP files + relational store) produced by the extractor, queried via the QL Datalog-like language; not a general-purpose DB like Postgres/SQLite
tools.parser: compiler-integrated extraction (NOT tree-sitter, NOT a generic AST, NOT an LSP) -- the key differentiator from every other tool in this survey
tools.embeddings: no
sidecars: none beyond the extractor invoking the real language toolchain during a build
tools.install: CodeQL CLI download (GitHub-distributed binary) + github/codeql query packs via the CLI's pack manager; VS Code extension for interactive query authoring
tools.local: yes, runs locally (CLI) or as part of GitHub's cloud code-scanning product
tools.licence: MIT for the github/codeql queries/libraries repo; the CLI extractor/evaluator engine itself is proprietary/closed-source, governed by a separate CodeQL Terms of Service
tools.languages_claimed: ~10-12 (C/C++, C#, Go, Java/Kotlin, JS/TS, Python, Ruby, Rust, Swift per GitHub's supported-languages docs; exact current count unverified this pass)
tools.cross_service: no -- single-codebase security/quality analysis, not cross-service route mapping
tools.deps_mapping: yes, but for security dataflow (taint tracking through call/data paths), not general dependency/HTTP mapping
tools.resource_complaints: issue #16780 'Don't divide CODEQL_RAM in half'; issue #19374 '[JAVA][GRADLE] OOM Issue with GitHub Autobuilder for Kotlin'; issue #14138 'SIGSEGV (code 134) during Finalizing database step'

tools.name: GitHub stack-graphs
tools.runtime: library (Rust crate), not a standalone end-user CLI/daemon -- consumed by other tools (e.g. GitHub's own precise-code-navigation product)
storage: none built into the OSS crates themselves (in-memory graph construction); persistence is left to the consumer
tools.parser: tree-sitter-stack-graphs bridges tree-sitter parse trees into stack-graph name-binding rules (per-language .tsg rule files in the languages/ dir); resolution itself uses the stack-graphs algorithm, a graph-based, LSP-independent name/scope-resolution technique
tools.embeddings: no
sidecars: none -- pure library
tools.install: Cargo (Rust crate dependency) -- not an end-user install
tools.local: yes -- runs wherever its host process runs
tools.languages_claimed: a handful of languages/ configs shipped in-repo (exact count unverified this pass); used most prominently for Python on github.com's own code navigation
tools.deps_mapping: yes, for cross-file/cross-module name resolution within a single language's semantics (the core stack-graphs use case), not HTTP/service mapping
tools.resource_complaints: none found/applicable -- library, not an end-user tool with its own issue reports of this kind

rust_note: Yes, Rust is a real and growing choice among code-intel peers, though not universal. Confirmed in this survey: ast-grep (core+LSP crate), CodeGraph's parsing kernel (codegraph-kernel, via napi-rs, with automatic WASM/JS fallback), GitHub's stack-graphs (+tree-sitter-stack-graphs), and stack-graphs powers parts of github.com's own precise code navigation. Zed editor (not in this survey's tool list but the standard reference point) is written in Rust for its GPUI/editor core. Published advantages cited by these projects are consistent rather than benchmarked head-to-head against Go: (1) native speed with no GC pauses for parse-heavy hot loops (ast-grep, codegraph-kernel's stated design goal of 'one JS boundary crossing per file' to avoid marshalling overhead), (2) memory-safety without a runtime/GC, letting a Rust core embed inside a JS/Node host as a napi addon (codegraph-kernel) or inside any host process as a library (stack-graphs) rather than needing its own process, and (3) LTO+single-codegen-unit release builds (both ast-grep's and codegraph-kernel's Cargo.toml set lto=true) as a common perf lever. None of the sources fetched in this pass published a direct Rust-vs-Go microbenchmark; the advantage claims found are architectural/qualitative, not measured comparisons. Fathom's own choice (pure Go + tree-sitter-via-wazero/WASM) sidesteps the CGO/native-toolchain distribution cost that both CodeGraph (ships a Rust napi addon with WASM fallback) and GitNexus (needs pnpm --allow-build / a C++ toolchain for some native grammars) explicitly have to solve for. Sources: https://github.com/ast-grep/ast-grep (Cargo.toml), https://github.com/colbymchenry/codegraph (codegraph-kernel/Cargo.toml, README 'Built for speed - the Rust kernel'), https://github.com/github/stack-graphs.
